summary: Shinobu Arai Apple works in Buddhist studies. She studied under Mark Csikszentmihalyi in 2000, Robert Bickner as academic adviser, and Charles Hallisey as her doctoral supervisor (attested 2003).
Shinobu Yamaguchi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned her PhD from Nagoya University in 1995 and was attested as a professor at Toyo University in 2015.

Shinsho Hanayama (1898–1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Fourth Higher School and the University of Tokyo (~1920–1923). He taught Buddhism at the University of Tokyo (~1934–1959) and served as professor at Toyo University (~1959) and Kokugakuin University.

Shintaro Kitano is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under supervisor Kazunobu Matsuda (attested 2005). He held posts as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2005) and part-time lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 2015).
Shinten Sakai is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Shindo Shiraishi and held a post at Koyasan University (attested 1959).

Shinya Mano works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He served as a part-time lecturer at Waseda University (attested 2015–2019) and as a research associate at SOAS University of London (attested 2019).

Shinya Moriyama (born 1972) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed graduate studies at the University of Tokyo (~1996–1998) and the University of Vienna (~2000–2006, Dr.Phil), studying under Eli Franco in 2002, and held a post at Shinshu University (~2011).

Shiro Matsumoto (born 1950) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology who studied at Waseda, Komazawa, and Tokyo universities under Yasuaki Nara and Zuiho Yamaguchi. He served as professor at Komazawa University (1995–2020) and visiting professor at the University of Chicago (2001).

Shiv Nath Sharma was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He held a post at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir (attested 1947), and served as a professor at St. Andrew's College, Gorakhpur (attested 1973).

Shiv Singh is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya (2018–2024) and held a postdoctoral researcher post at the Indian Council of Social Science Research in 2026.

Shivram Dattatray Joshi (1926–2013) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (~1960–1964) and held posts as professor and director at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1964–1986) and head of the Sanskrit Dictionary Department at Deccan College (~1987–1993).

Shizuka Sasaki (born 1956) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Kyoto University (~1975–1987) under Jikido Takasaki, UC Berkeley (1988), and Bukkyo University (PhD, 1999). He was appointed Professor of Indian Buddhism at Hanazono University in 2002.

Shlomo Pines (1908–1990) was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Heidelberg, Geneva, and Berlin (Promotion, 1926–1934), later teaching at the University of Paris and serving as philosophy professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1952–1990).

Shmuel Sambursky (1900–1990) specialized in philosophy, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Königsberg (~1920–1923) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1923–1924), and held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1928–1970).

Shobha Rani Dash specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She was an open-recruitment researcher at Ryukoku University (2010), a lecturer at Otani University (attested 2012), and a professor at Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).

Shobhana Gokhale (1928–2013) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. She was a faculty member at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute and director at Bharat Itihas Sanshodhak Mandal (attested 2006).
Shodo Fujita (born 1959) is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Ryukoku University under Shoko Takeuchi. He served as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University (attested 1995–2013).

Shodo Harada (born 1940) is a Buddhist studies figure who trained at Shofuku-ji (~1964–1984) under Mumon Yamada (1962–1982). He became abbot of Sōgen-ji in 1982 and founded the Tahoma Sogenji Zen Monastery in 1995.

Shodo Yamakami (born 1939) is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University (~1961–1964) and served as assistant professor (~1974–1988) and professor (~1988–2008) at Kyoto Sangyo University.

Shogo Watanabe (born 1953) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Toyo University. He served as professor at Toyo University (~1999–2024) and held posts at Taisho University and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).
